entry.idea: Lovable lets anyone describe an app in plain English and its AI writes the code, builds it, and puts a working piece of software online.
entry.lesson: Once a technology crosses a usability threshold, put a simple chat box in front of it and let ordinary people become builders.
entry.name: Lovable

growth.reason: Going from $1M to $100M in annual revenue in 8 months with 2.3 million users is an extremely fast, well-documented growth curve.

market.reason: Anyone who wants a piece of software built, from solo founders to large businesses, is a potential customer, which is close to the whole software market.

tech.reason: Lovable built a strong 'describe it and it builds' product on top of existing AI models, but well-funded rivals like Bolt and Replit could match it within a year or two.

entry.twist: It grew from $1 million to $100 million a year in revenue in just eight months, which people are calling the fastest a software company has ever grown.
entry.who_pays: People and businesses pay a subscription to build, host and run their apps on Lovable.
entry.why_now: AI models got good enough at writing and testing code that people who cannot program can now describe an app and get a real, working one back.
